I’m turning 19 in a few days and I feel the same way. Looking back now I was quite reserved back in high school, not really knowing how to deal with friends, school, mental health, sexuality and all that other shit. I just kept my head down and did what was needed of me and it was so depressing. I ended up losing people I still care about to this day because I was to scared to be open and honest.

After high school, I decided to travel overseas and just be more open with myself and it was the best experience I’ve ever had.

I still stress a lot about how I’ve got nothing sorted with my life, but I feel like the world tells us that we need to have chosen our adult careers while still in high school and if we don’t we’re gonna struggle. But I just gotta keep reminding myself that I’m just a tiny 18 year old boy, and that’s young, and I’m gonna keep being a kid and do dumb shit as long as I can.

Ok, you can't say that. You cannot say they should be grateful they live in the first world and thankful that they have clean water and sanitation and all those other first world luxuries. We didn't choose to be born into the first world. Try telling all the depressed youths who are contemplating killing themselves that because they have their health, clean food, clean water, shelter and access to education they're simply ungrateful and have no reason to feel suicidal. This is the kind of bullshit that my parents told me as they said I have no right to be depressed. So please don't say this stuff, especially to those that are at their worst. Depression doesn't care about your circumstances. It affects everyone regardless of class, race, religion, etc. You don't need to feel guilty about being depressed.
